title: Distinct vertices of a critical graph have incomparable neighbourhoods
statement: Let $G$ be a critical graph on a finite, nonempty vertex set, so that $\chi(H) < \chi(G)$ for every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$. Then for any two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$, the neighbourhood $N(u)$ is not contained in the neighbourhood $N(v)$.
hypotheses_covered: u and v are distinct vertices
replaced:
\emph{Show that if \texttt{u} and \texttt{v} are two
vertices of a critical graph \texttt{G}, then \texttt{N(u) $\not\subset$ N(v)}.}
